claims.tolerance: Nearest integer for the article’s approximate AIC; 1766 is materially different from 1722.
claims.cause: Shipped formula uses R formula nesting rather than the intended arithmetic proportion.
claims.evidence: https://osf.io/download/6a216eefee84266e775b8113/ section 2.3 (p.7) and Table 3 (p.8); likelihood-only row. Pinned E3_analysis.R contains the corresponding executable lmer/AIC expression at lines 239-240; the source uses the same formula.
claims.rationale: The original article prints approximately 1722, whereas the source obtains 1766.298 from the original model predictions and AIC procedure. This is separate from the later RMSE-versus-MAE robustness comparison. Pilot diagnostics explain the discrepancy: R parses (t/(t+f)) as terms t and t:f. Protecting the arithmetic with I() gives AIC 1721.98145543401; the Sol pilot independently gets 1721.9814554340073 using the precomputed Proportion variable and documented mixed-effects option. Both diagnostics change how the predictor is specified relative to the executable nested expression and are non-scoring.

notes: C1-C5 target the printed numerical heuristic-comparison paragraph on p.1021, not values extracted from the Figure 8 fixed-effects bars. The paper describes Figure 8 as fixed effects but the source Table 3 reports mixed-effects values. C1/C2 are executable lmer expressions in the pinned script. C3-C5 follow the authors' explicit mixed-effects instruction (add participant/item random intercepts and use lmer), instantiated by the reproducer; their references are scoped to that documented intended procedure, not the default lm/dredge branch. No equivalence of fixed- and mixed-effects models is asserted. The 1722-versus-1766.298 difference remains a P2 discrepancy in the shipped heuristic expression. No RMSE/MAE robustness specification supplies these references. v1.1 adds both pilot explanations for C1 as explicitly non-scoring diagnostics. They converge on an arithmetic-proportion mixed model; merely switching between fixed and mixed effects does not itself establish the shipped expression is correct. No C1 status, severity, or scoring-reference change is made.
